title: How Much of a Cabin Move Co-Payment the Traveller Settles under a Corporate Travel Programmes Reference
content:
Where a corporate programme reference stands on an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking, part of the co-payment for a cabin move falls to the Corporate Travel Programmes side rather than to the traveller, and the payment terms of that programme decide how much.

## 1. What is collected from the traveller

| Where | What is collected from the traveller is |
| --- | --- |
| a corporate programme reference stands on the booking and the programme's payment terms run 30 days or more | 0.75 of the figure, being 75 percent of it |
| a corporate programme reference stands on the booking and the programme's payment terms run fewer than 30 days | 0.9 of the figure, being 90 percent of it |
| in every other case | no such treatment applies to what is collected |

The payment terms read are the terms in days of the Corporate Travel Programmes programme the reference on the booking names. A booking with no such reference never falls on either of the first two rows.

## 2. Boundary readings, on hypothetical figures

A programme whose payment terms run exactly 30 days is at 30 days or more, so 75 percent of the figure is collected from the traveller; one whose terms run 29 days falls to the second row, and 90 percent is collected.

On a figure of 586.50 USD, a programme on 45-day terms collects 439.88 USD from the traveller once rounded to the nearest cent, and a programme on 14-day terms collects 527.85 USD.

A booking with no corporate programme reference standing on it falls to the third row.
